documents.text:
## Limitations

- **Only running jobs are cancelled.** A request for a job that is not
  running when the workers receive it has no effect, even if the job starts
  right after.
- **Cancellation is cooperative.** A processor that ignores the signal runs
  to the end.
- **A job can finish first.** A request that arrives once the job is
  completed has no effect.
- **No confirmation.** `publish()` tells you how many workers received the
  request, not whether one of them was running the job.
- **A worker that is removed** (frozen or disconnected for longer than the
  relay's `leaseDuration`) misses the request. By then its job has most
  likely been moved back to the queue as stalled.

## Delivery guarantees

A message is written to the inboxes of the nodes that are subscribed **at the
moment it is published**, in the same atomic operation that resolves the
subscriptions. From there:

- **Brief disconnections are covered.** If a node loses its connection, the
  messages published meanwhile wait in its inbox and are delivered when it
  reconnects.
- **Removed nodes lose their messages.** If a node stops renewing its lease
  (it crashed, or was frozen for longer than `leaseDuration`), it is removed
  with its subscriptions and inbox. See
  [Nodes and failures](nodes-and-failures.md).
- **A node that can't keep up loses its oldest messages.** Each inbox keeps
  at most `inboxMaxLength` unread messages. See
  [Slow subscribers](#slow-subscribers).
- **Subscriptions only see what comes after them.** Subscribing does not
  replay earlier messages, except the topic's
  [retained message](retained-messages.md).

In other words, the Relay is for live messages. It is not a log: when a
message must be processed reliably and with retries, use a queue. Queues
process jobs at least once (for example, a stalled job can be processed again
by another worker), so processors must tolerate duplicates.

request.instructions: The documents are sections of the documentation of ONE open-source project at one commit. Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).
